content: Integrin alpha-11 (ITGA11) is a protein in humans encoded by the ITGA11 gene. This gene produces an alpha integrin, which is a component of integrins—heterodimeric integral membrane proteins composed of an alpha chain and a beta chain. The ITGA11 protein contains an I domain and is expressed in muscle tissue. It has been shown to dimerize with beta-1 integrin in vitro and appears to bind collagen in this dimerized form. This suggests that ITGA11 may play a role in anchoring muscle tissue to the extracellular matrix. Alternative transcriptional splice variants of the ITGA11 gene have been identified, but their biological significance remains unclear. One study has reported that ITGA11 expression is elevated in the anterior stroma of corneal buttons excised from eyes affected by keratoconus, a degenerative eye disorder.
